title: Adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference system for customizing investment type based on the potential investors' demographics and feedback
authors: Asemi, A.; Asemi, A.; Ko, A.
tldr: An ANFIS-based recommender system uses demographic data and fuzzy inference to suggest investment types for potential investors.
problem_and_motivation: Investment recommender systems rarely leverage demographic information and fuzzy logic to personalize investment type recommendations for potential investors. Existing systems focus on specific areas like stock portfolios or hedge funds without addressing how demographic factors influence investment preferences. There is a gap in using adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference to combine expert knowledge with investor feedback for personalized investment guidance.
approach: K-Means clustering groups 1542 survey respondents into three investment type clusters based on their investment product preferences.
ANFIS with Sugeno fuzzy inference uses six demographic inputs (gender, age, location, education, job, income) to recommend investment types.
Hybrid learning algorithm trains the ANFIS network with 1542 data pairs over three epochs, generating 1296 fuzzy rules.
Expert knowledge supplements system-generated rules, allowing investment professionals to modify or add rules based on domain expertise.
Investor feedback loop enables iterative system improvement by identifying weak recommendations and correcting errors.
findings: num: Three investment type clusters were identified: Cluster 1 (592 respondents), Cluster 2 (406 respondents), Cluster 3 (340 respondents).
num: DemographicANFIS system achieved average testing error of 0.86683 with 2647 nodes and 1365 parameters.
num: 1296 fuzzy rules were generated from 1542 training data pairs using grid partition.
Cluster 1 investors prefer government securities, mutual funds, and listed stock without recent stock market experience.
Higher income investors tend to be assigned to investment clusters with more aggressive investment products.
The system operates with incomplete or inaccurate data using fuzzy logic functions.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper introduces an ANFIS-based investment recommender system that combines demographic profiling with fuzzy inference to suggest investment types. It demonstrates that six demographic factors (gender, age, location, education, job, income) can effectively predict investment preferences when processed through adaptive neuro-fuzzy inference. The system generates 1296 fuzzy rules from 1542 training pairs, incorporating both data-driven rules and expert knowledge. The feedback mechanism enables continuous improvement, and the system's ability to operate with incomplete data addresses real-world data quality challenges in financial applications.
directly_justifies: ANFIS with six demographic inputs generates 1296 fuzzy rules for investment type recommendation.
K-Means clustering identifies three distinct investor groups based on investment product preferences.
Hybrid learning with three epochs achieves average testing error of 0.86683 on the validation set.
Expert knowledge integration allows investment professionals to modify or add rules to the system.
The system operates effectively with incomplete or inaccurate data using fuzzy logic functions.
limits: The system considers only six demographic variables as inputs, potentially missing other relevant factors.
Investment type outputs are limited to three clusters, reducing granularity of recommendations.
The study uses Hungarian data from 2019, limiting generalizability to other markets and time periods.
The average testing error of 0.86683 suggests room for improvement in prediction accuracy.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: All 14 topic domains were systematically scanned. High relevance was assigned to financial behavioral profiles (5.A) and classification approaches (5.C) as the paper's core contribution is demographic-based investor profiling using K-Means and ANFIS. Medium relevance was assigned to profile dynamics (5.B) for cold-start through demographics, predictive modeling (6.A) for ANFIS-based prediction, engagement dynamics (11.A) for the feedback loop, and existing systems landscape (4.A) and gaps (4.B) for the literature review. Topics rejected include expense categorization (3.A-3.C) as the paper deals with investment types not expenses, budgeting strategies (7.A-7.D), anomaly detection (8.A-8.C), mobile design (9.A-9.C), data privacy (10.A mentioned only in passing), savings/debt management (13.A-13.C), and synthetic data generation (14.A). The paper's topical coverage centers on demographic-based investor profiling and fuzzy inference for investment recommendations.
